school_lunch_dish_ages_6_to_11: 10 to 15 g (not 20 g); rice adds about 8.7 g
basis: Lunch share of the 2026 recommendation is 9.6 to 19.6 g across ages 6 to 11; published lunches already carry 31.8 g
notes: TPP-04 uses 20 g, an adult canteen figure.

school_lunch_dish_ages_6_to_11: DIAAS at least 75 on the young-child pattern for the product, or a blend with meat, egg or milk
complementary_food_ages_6_to_23_months: DIAAS at least 75 on the young-child pattern; animal-source or milk protein preferred by current evidence
basis: FAO claim thresholds as reported in NQR-05; tofu 64 to 84 and soy flour 77 on the young-child pattern
notes: A soy concentrate or soy-cereal blend can reach it; wheat gluten cannot.

school_lunch_dish_ages_6_to_11: 3 to 5 mg added zinc per serving (zinc oxide or sulphate) if the dish replaces meat or fish
complementary_food_ages_6_to_23_months: 4 to 5 mg per 40 to 50 g daily dose (supplement guidance)
basis: Closes the 0.73 to 1.85 mg gap of a meatless lunch at age 6 to 7 and most of it at 10 to 11; trial doses 5 to 5.6 mg
notes: Stay below the 2026 upper limits for zinc (values not retrieved).

school_lunch_dish_ages_6_to_11: 2 to 3 mg per serving in a form that survives phytate (for example NaFeEDTA), or phytase-treated soy
basis: Lunch share at 10% absorption is 2.2 to 4.5 mg; soy phytate to iron molar ratio about 9.9 against a target below 1
notes: Iron is the harder nutrient: the Thai seasoning trial did not move anaemia.

school_lunch_dish_ages_6_to_11: at most 300 mg per serving (about 15 mg per g of protein)
basis: Half the lunch sodium allowance of 540 to 720 mg at age 6 to 7; frozen analogues carry about 686 mg per 20 g of protein
notes: Our choice of half the lunch allowance.

school_lunch_dish_ages_6_to_11: not needed at two plant days a week; add if the product replaces animal food daily
notes: The online 2026 lookup lists no B12 value for these ages (NQR-01).
